A model and its morphisms mean the functors and natural transformations in [lem-coef-finite-limit-sketch-models]; no presentability conclusion of that node is used. Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. For each specified product or pullback vertex $T$ of a model $M$, the function taking an element of $M(T)$ to its tuple of projections is a bijection onto the corresponding product or compatible-tuples set: existence and uniqueness are exactly the limit-cone condition. In particular $M(B)$ identifies with $M(O)^2$, $M(p_n)$ with $(M(s_n),M(t_n))$, parallel pairs with pairs in a common fiber, and composable pairs with pairs $b,a$ satisfying $s(b)=t(a)$. proof.text: For a model $M$, set $\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C_M)=M(O)$ and $\mathcal C_M(x,y)^n=\{a\in M(A_n):s_n(a)=x,\ t_n(a)=y\}$. Define zero by $M(z_n)$ at the unique point of $M(B)$ over $(x,y)$, and restrict negation, scalars and addition to this fiber using step 1. Endpoint preservation makes these operations well-defined. Evaluating each module equation of [lem-coef-dgcat-finite-limit-sketch-signature] on a tuple in this fiber proves the corresponding $R$-module axiom. Likewise $M(d_n)$ restricts to an $R$-linear map to degree $n+1$, and $d_{n+1}d_n=z_{n+2}p_n$ says on each element that its second differential is zero. All these sets are $\mathcal U$-small, being subsets of values of $M$.

proof.text: For $a\in\mathcal C_M(x,y)^p$ and $b\in\mathcal C_M(y,z)^q$, use the unique composable-pair lift of $(b,a)$ from step 1 and apply $M(c_{q,p})$ to define $ba\in\mathcal C_M(x,z)^{p+q}$. Define $1_x=M(1)(x)$. Evaluate the signature equations on composable triples and on parallel/composable tuples: they give associativity, both unit identities and bilinearity. The differential equations give $d(1_x)=0$ and $d(ba)=d(b)a+(-1)^q b\,d(a)$, with $q=|b|$ as required. Thus steps 2 and 3 give precisely the dg-category data and axioms in the statement. No homotopy or quasi-equivalence is involved.

proof.text: Given a model morphism $\alpha:M\to N$, take its object map $\alpha_O$ and send a homogeneous arrow $a$ to $\alpha_{A_n}(a)$. Naturality for $s_n,t_n$ puts this arrow in $\mathcal C_N(\alpha_Ox,\alpha_Oy)^n$. Naturality for projections forces $\alpha_T$ on each auxiliary vertex to send each projected tuple to its componentwise image: compare all projections and use uniqueness in the target limit. Naturality for zero, addition, scalars, differential, composition and unit arrows therefore says exactly that these fiber maps are linear chain maps preserving composition and units. They define a strict dg functor. Identities and composites are preserved since their components on $O$ and $A_n$ are respectively identities and composites of functions. Denote this functor on model categories by $E$.

proof.text: Conversely, for a small $R$-linear dg category $\mathcal C$ set $D(\mathcal C)(O)=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $D(\mathcal C)(A_n)=\coprod_{x,y}\mathcal C(x,y)^n$; use the two labels for endpoints. Interpret $B$, parallel pairs, composable pairs and every further tuple sort by their actual finite products or pullbacks of sets. Interpret the operation arrows by the labeled module operations, differential, units and composition of $\mathcal C$. Interpret every tuple arrow by the tuple of its prescribed projections. The dg axioms give exactly the listed equations, and substituting a well-typed expression preserves each equation. Hence paths of generating arrows with equal class induce equal functions; this defines a functor on the presented indexing category. The designated cones are limit cones by construction, so this is a model. Every sort is $\mathcal U$-small: labeled unions are indexed by a $\mathcal U$-small set of object pairs and all auxiliary sorts are finite limits of $\mathcal U$-small sets.

proof.text: For a strict dg functor $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, define $D(F)_O=F$ on objects and $D(F)_{A_n}(x,y,a)=(Fx,Fy,F(a))$. On auxiliary sorts use componentwise maps of compatible tuples. A source composable pair remains composable because its common endpoint has the same image under $F$; no injectivity of $F$ is required. Preservation of module operations, differential, units and composition verifies naturality for every operation arrow; the componentwise formulas verify it for projections and tuple arrows. Naturality for arbitrary paths follows by composing these squares, and the relations impose no further condition. Componentwise formulas also preserve identities and composites, defining the functor $D$ from dg categories to models.

proof.text: For every $\mathcal C$, the functor $E D(\mathcal C)\to\mathcal C$ is the identity on objects and on each degree sends the element $(x,y,a)$ of the fiber over $(x,y)$ to $a$. Its inverse inserts the labels $(x,y)$; these are mutually inverse linear chain maps preserving composition and units by their definitions. For $F:\mathcal C\to\mathcal D$, both routes around the naturality square send $(x,y,a)$ to $F(a)$ and send $x$ to $Fx$. Thus these isomorphisms are natural in $\mathcal C$.

proof.text: For a model $M$, define $\eta_M:M\to D E(M)$ on $O$ by the identity and on $A_n$ by $a\mapsto(s_n(a),t_n(a),a)$. The inverse forgets the two labels. On each auxiliary sort use its projection-tuple bijection from step 1, followed by these primary-sort bijections; its inverse is the unique lift of the corresponding tuple to $M$. These formulas commute with projections. They commute with operation arrows because the operations of $E(M)$ were defined using those same unique tuple lifts; for a tuple arrow, equality follows by comparing its prescribed projections. They consequently commute with all paths and give an isomorphism of models. For $\alpha:M\to N$, naturality on $A_n$ reads $a\mapsto(\alpha_Os_n(a),\alpha_Ot_n(a),\alpha_{A_n}(a))$ on both sides, by endpoint naturality. Naturality on every auxiliary sort follows by comparing projections. Thus $\eta$ is a natural isomorphism. Together with step 7 this proves the claimed equivalence. Its evaluation comparisons are the identity on $O$ and the displayed label-insertion/forgetting bijections on $A_n$, natural for arbitrary object maps.

title: Models of the dg-category sketch are dg categories
statement: Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal V$ as in [def-weil-size-convention] and a commutative ring $R\in\mathcal U$. Let $S_R$ be the explicit signature sketch of [lem-coef-dgcat-finite-limit-sketch-signature], with object sort $O$, degree-$n$ arrow sort $A_n$ and endpoint maps $s_n,t_n$. Its category of models in $\operatorname{Set}_{\mathcal U}$, with natural transformations as morphisms, is equivalent to the ordinary category of $R$-linear dg categories and strict dg functors, where a dg category has a $\mathcal U$-small object set, $\mathbf Z$-graded $\mathcal U$-small $R$-module morphism groups, a degree-$1$ square-zero differential, associative unital $R$-bilinear composition and $d(ba)=d(b)a+(-1)^{|b|}b\,d(a)$; a strict dg functor is an object map and linear chain maps preserving units and composition. The functor from models takes the object set to be $M(O)$ and $\mathcal C_M(x,y)^n=(M(s_n),M(t_n))^{-1}(x,y)$, with operations induced by the sketch. The inverse takes $O=\operatorname{Ob}(\mathcal C)$ and $A_n=\coprod_{x,y}\mathcal C(x,y)^n$ and interprets every product or pullback sort as its actual finite limit of sets. The induced maps on model morphisms are the object and homogeneous-arrow maps of the corresponding strict dg functor. The two functors are inverse up to natural isomorphism, with their isomorphisms given by fiber decomposition and the canonical product and pullback identifications. In particular, evaluations on $O$ and $A_n$ correspond respectively to object sets and disjoint unions of homogeneous morphisms, for arbitrary object maps.
